Credit data: bureaus (CICs) and the Account Aggregator

After this lesson you can:
  • Explain what a bureau pull is, its permissible-purpose rule and what it returns
  • Describe the Account Aggregator consent artefact and data flow
  • Contrast bureau data with cash-flow data in underwriting

Learning rhythm: read one section at a time, pause to explain the control in your own words, then answer the knowledge check without looking back.

On this page
  1. The bureau: borrowing history on demand
  2. The Account Aggregator: consented cash-flow data
  3. Facts, not vibes
  4. Regulatory anchors
  5. Where this lives in LoanOS
  6. Knowledge check

1. The bureau: borrowing history on demand

India has four licensed Credit Information Companies. A bureau pull requires a permissible purpose and borrower consent, and returns the credit report: score, active and closed trade lines, current obligations (the EMIs the person already pays), delinquency history, past write-offs or settlements, and recent enquiry counts.

Underwriting reads that report in structured ways: score bands and policy knockouts (a recent write-off may be an automatic decline), obligation extraction for affordability, enquiry velocity as a stress signal, and thin-file rules for people with little history. Remember the loop: after disbursement the RE reports this very loan back to the CICs — module 9 covers the reporting duty.

2. The Account Aggregator: consented cash-flow data

The AA framework is India's consent rail for financial data.

The borrower approves a consent artefact — machine-readable, specifying purpose, the financial-information types, one-time or periodic fetch, validity period and data-life (how long the recipient may keep it).

Data then flows from the FIP (the bank holding the account) via the licensed AA to the RE as FIU — encrypted, never seen by the AA itself, India-resident.

Bank statements via AA power cash-flow underwriting: income detection and stability, existing EMI outflows, bounce incidence, balance behaviour. This reaches borrowers whom bureau files underserve — and every derived analytic must retain provenance back to the consented fetch.

3. Facts, not vibes

In LoanOS, whatever the source — bureau, AA, GST/ITR verification, employer checks — data enters the decision as verified facts with provenance: what was fetched, when, under which consent, from which provider.

The decision engine consumes those facts; it does not reach out to fetch anything itself.

That separation (facts gathered by workflows, judged by policy) is what makes every decision explainable and replayable.

Regulatory anchors

  • RBI-CIR-2025 — Credit information reporting directions — the same CIC relationship that supplies bureau reports.
  • RBI-AA-2016 — Account Aggregator framework: consent artefact, FIP→AA→FIU flow, India residency.
  • DPDP-2023 — Purpose-bound consent governs every data fetch used in underwriting.

Family IDs resolve in the India regulatory register (docs/compliance/india-regulatory-register.md), which owns sources and caveats.

Where this lives in LoanOS

  • Capability UWG-001 — Bureau pull with permissible purpose and consent.
  • Capability UWG-005 — Account Aggregator consent and FI fetch.
  • Capability UWG-007 — Bank-statement categorisation, stability, bounce and cash-flow analysis.
  • Code packages/core/src/integrations/account-aggregator.js — AA consent module: artefact lifecycle and evidence.

Retrieval practice

Knowledge check

Answer aloud or write your choice before opening the explanation. If you miss it, revisit the named section—not the whole lesson.

1. What does the AA consent artefact NOT contain?

  1. Purpose of the fetch
  2. Validity period and data-life
  3. The borrower's account balance
  4. Financial-information types covered
Reveal answer and reasoning

C. The artefact is the permission, not the data: it defines purpose, scope, fetch type, validity and data-life; the data flows separately, encrypted end-to-end.

2. Why must derived analytics (e.g. detected income) retain provenance?

  1. For marketing attribution
  2. So the decision can be explained and replayed from consented source data
  3. To bill the FIP
  4. Provenance is optional
Reveal answer and reasoning

B. Decision lineage requires every input fact to trace to its consented, timestamped source — that is what makes an audit answerable.
